title: Dependency authority: resolve before target mutation
summary: Dependency resolution remains pre-mutation authority. Production ooRexx release deployment now prefers SSC qualified sealed module deployments with exact dependency deployment ids; Deployment then materialises those semantic bytes into a deterministic target namespace. Legacy SSC_MANIFEST/@source-requires/::requires closure remains a development/archive intake path, while native/runtime capabilities remain ordinary Deployment requirements.
invariants: Dependencies are resolved before target mutation.
For production releases, qualified SSC deployment ids and sealed dependency ids are preferred semantic authority.
Development/archive intake may use SSC_MANIFEST, @source-requires and reachable ::requires, but must not be described as sealed deployment authority.
Semantic source closure, package-load edges, target namespace and native/runtime capabilities are different evidence classes.
REXX_PATH is produced after resolution as explicit launch state; ambient REXX_PATH is not dependency authority.
A DeploymentManifest that declares dependencies but lacks a satisfied dependency resolution/lock must fail before executable actions are planned.
Non-ooRexx dependencies such as libc, compiler, native loadability and ffmpeg capability remain ordinary Deployment requirements rather than being forced into SSC.

provenance.claim: Defines sealed-vs-development dependency authority and deterministic namespace rules.
Executable documentation for current dependency authority split and target namespace.
